subject: Starting to use own audio files

messages.author: 058fe95fdf276f0f
messages.subject: Starting to use own audio files
parts:
Hey guys,

I'm new to Seewave R package, and have never worked with R language before.

I've got already done some of the examples We can found on the internet, but now I need to process my own audio files, which are recorded as *.wav files.

Where am I suppose to store my *.wav files in order to have them read and worked. I have noticed all the examples We can work on are stored in R Workspace formats.

Any practical guidance someone could give me?

messages.author: 44c03a0165efd08f
messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Starting to use own audio files
parts:
Hi Tiago,

In general the process is the same as loading any file into R. You use a specific function (here it would be readWave()) and tell it where to look for the file.

File locations trip up a lot of new R users. I would suggest checking out some tutorials which explain the ideas of a working directory, and projects (if you're using Rstudio). This resource looks like a good place to start: https://www.stat.ubc.ca/~jenny/STAT545A/block01_basicsWorkspaceWorkingDirProject.html#workspace-and-working-directory

Once you understand how to refer to the location of a file, you need to use the readWave() function which is explained here: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/seewave/vignettes/seewave_IO.pdf#subsubsection.1.3.1

I hope this helps get you started,

Steffi

Dr. Stefanie LaZerte
Biologist, R and CitSci Enthusiast
http://steffilazerte.ca/

seewave::spectro(tico)

Do I have to transform the *.wav file into any other format of file?

It seems I have understood how SeeWave functions but I'm missing the basic even taking a loog at the guides We can found on the internet.
